newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Piltel, Philcom sharpen up with share swap.
newsitem.headline: Piltel, Philcom sharpen up with share swap.

text.p: A planned share swap by two of the Philippines' largest telecommunication companies is expected to help equip both for the increasingly competitive local market, analysts said on Thursday.

Pilipino Telephone Corp (Piltel), the country's largest mobile phone company, and Philippine Global Communication (Philcom), the second biggest international gateway operator, said earlier they had agreed a 20 percent stake swap.
Piltel will sell 258.25 million unissued common shares to Philcom at a minimum price of 20 pesos each, making the deal worth at least 5.17 billion pesos ($193.7 million).
In return Piltel has an option to acquire a 20 percent interest in Philcom after its proposed initial public offering.
"The deal is a fund-raising exercise for Piltel," said Raul Ruiz, vice-president at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
Bernard Gorospe, analyst at Citisecurities Inc, said the swap will help Piltel raise cash for its telephone programme in the Mindanao region in the southern Philippines.
In turn, Philcom will have a stake in the lucrative cellular phone business.
Under Philippine law, cellular phone companies must install 400,000 land lines, while international gateway operators are mandated to build 300,000 lines in exchange for their permits.
Most of the companies, including Piltel, have to complete the installations by 1998.
"Piltel's cloning problems will not be resolved even if Philcom is around, but they definitely will need the cash stemming from the swap deal," Gorospe said.
Piltel has been battered by problems of illegal cloning of mobile phones which led to a 10-fold increase in provisions for doubtful accounts of 886.35 million pesos last year.
Analysts said they expected the proposed deal to help the two firms speed up the installation of their required telephone lines.
The National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) has assigned a service area to Piltel in Mindanao adjacent to Philcom's area.
"There will be economies of scale. They can get assistance from one another and pool their resources in rolling out those lines," said Alexis Cabel, analyst at Angping & Associates Securities.
"We still recommend a long-term buy on Piltel as we like its latest move to become a more complete telecom firm."
Sun Hung Kai's Ruiz said Piltel can now have access to the international gateway facility of Philcom without the need to install the usually required 300,000 lines.
Piltel closed 50 centavos higher on Wednesday at 14.75 pesos after reaching an intra-day high of 15 pesos. It was unchanged by mid-morning on Thursday.
Analysts said Philippine telecommunication companies are likely to pursue mergers because of the stiff domestic competition.
At present, there are 11 international gateway facility operators, five cellular phone companies, 12 paging companies and 11 local exchange carriers. ($1=26.66 pesos)
